DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Jane Smith | Age: 42 | DOS: 2026-09-10 | DOD: 2026-09-11
Procedure: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
Surgeon: Dr. Vance
Medications:
- Paracetamol 1000mg QDS PO for 7 days
- Ibuprofen 400mg TDS PO with meals for 5 days
- Tramadol 50mg PRN severe pain (max 200mg/day)
Instructions:
- Incision care: Keep dry 48 hrs. Showers permitted on Day 3. Pat dry.
- Activity: Light walking daily. No lifting over 10 lbs for 3 weeks.
- Diet: Low fat diet for 2 weeks.
Red Flags: Fever > 38.5C, jaundice (yellow eyes/skin), worsening right upper quadrant pain.
Follow-up: 2 weeks outpatient clinic.

restrictions: No lifting over 10 lbs for 3 weeks

ORTHOPEDIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Robert Taylor | Age: 68 | DOS: 2026-09-05 | DOD: 2026-09-08
Procedure: Left Total Knee Arthroplasty
Surgeon: Dr. Campbell
Medications:
- Rivaroxaban 10mg OD PO for 14 days (anticoagulation)
- Paracetamol 1g QDS regularly for 14 days
- Co-codamol 30/500 2 tablets QDS PRN for breakthrough pain
- Senna 15mg ON PRN for constipation
Instructions:
- Physical Therapy: Knee flexion exercises 3x daily. Full weight bearing with frame/crutches.
- Wound care: Aquacel dressing in place. Do not disturb until staple removal on Day 12.
- Ice operative knee 20 mins every 2 hours.
Red Flags: Calf swelling, unilateral leg warmth, sudden chest pain or shortness of breath (suspected DVT/PE), wound soakage or active bleeding.
Follow-up: Physiotherapy review Day 7. Orthopedic clinic Day 12 for staple removal.

DAY SURGERY DISCHARGE NOTE
Patient: David Miller | Age: 51 | Date: 2026-09-18
Procedure: Right Open Inguinal Hernia Repair with Mesh
Medications:
- Paracetamol 500mg: 2 tabs PO QDS x 5 days
- Naproxen 250mg: 1 tab PO BD with food x 5 days
Instructions:
- Ice groin area intermittently for first 24 hours.
- Wear supportive snug underwear (briefs, not boxers).
- Avoid straining, coughing, or heavy lifting (>5kg) for 4-6 weeks.
- Return to sedentary work in 1-2 weeks.
Red Flags: Inability to pass urine within 8 hours, scrotal hematoma/massive swelling, high fever (>38C).
Follow-up: GP review in 2 weeks.

SURGICAL SUMMARY
Patient: Emily Clark | Age: 29 | DOS: 2026-09-14 | DOD: 2026-09-15
Procedure: Emergency Laparoscopic Appendectomy (Complicated/Suppurative)
Medications:
- Co-amoxiclav 625mg TDS PO to complete 7-day course (5 days remaining)
- Paracetamol 1000mg QDS PO PRN pain
Instructions:
- Keep wounds covered for 48h. Showering allowed after 48h.
- Light diet for 2 days, then normal diet as tolerated.
- Avoid intense core exercises for 3 weeks.
Red Flags: Persistent fever > 38.2C, abdominal distension, severe persistent nausea/vomiting.
Follow-up: Routine surgical follow-up in 4 weeks.

restrictions: Avoid intense core exercises for 3 weeks

MATERNITY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Sarah Jenkins | Age: 34 | DOS: 2026-09-01 | DOD: 2026-09-03
Procedure: Elective Lower Segment Cesarean Section (LSCS)
Medications:
- Paracetamol 1g QDS PO for 7 days
- Ibuprofen 400mg TDS PO with food for 7 days
- Enoxaparin (Clexane) 40mg SubQ OD for 10 days
- Ferrous Fumarate 210mg OD PO for 30 days
Instructions:
- Keep dressing dry. Midwife to remove dressing Day 5.
- Check fundal height and lochia daily.
- Pelvic floor exercises may commence gently when comfortable.
- No lifting anything heavier than baby for 6 weeks.
Red Flags: Heavy vaginal bleeding (soaking >1 pad/hr), large clots, foul-smelling lochia, fever, severe calf pain.
Follow-up: Community midwife home visit Day 4 & Day 10. Postnatal 6-week check with GP.

restrictions: No lifting anything heavier than baby for 6 weeks
